entry.title: Atomic Habits: which parts to read
entry.summary: Worth it, but not cover to cover. 6 chapters carry the whole system; the rest repeats it with stories.

entry.title: Deep Work: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read rules 1, 2 and 4, skim the rest. Part 1 argues for focus at length; Part 2 tells you how to do it.

entry.title: Indistractable: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read parts 1, 2 and 4. They hold the whole method; the rest applies it to work, kids and relationships.

entry.title: Digital Minimalism: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read chapters 3, 4 and 6. The declutter plus what to fill the time with.

entry.title: Meditations: which parts to read
entry.summary: Start with Books 2, 4, 5 and 8. The other books repeat the same ideas in new words, which is the point, but not where to start.

entry.title: The Obstacle Is the Way: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read Parts 1 and 2. They turn Stoicism into a method: see clearly, then act.

entry.title: Four Thousand Weeks: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read the introduction, chapters 1, 2, 4 and 7, and the 10 tools at the end. That's the whole argument plus what to do with it.

entry.title: The Psychology of Money: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 6 of the 20 short chapters. They hold the ideas that change how you spend and save.

entry.title: I Will Teach You to Be Rich: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read chapters 4, 5 and 6 wherever you live. Much of the rest is built around US banks, cards and accounts.

entry.title: Your Money or Your Life: which parts to read
entry.summary: Do steps 2, 3, 4 and 8. They turn money into hours of your life, which changes how small buys feel.

entry.title: The Power of Habit: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read chapters 1 to 5 and the appendix. The rest is about companies and social movements: good stories, less to use.

entry.title: Tiny Habits: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read chapters 1, 3, 4 and 5. They hold the whole method; the rest grows it and applies it to bad habits and groups.

entry.title: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 6 of the 20 chapters. They make the whole case for low-cost index funds; the rest backs it up with more data. Chapters follow the 2017 10th anniversary edition.

entry.title: Essentialism: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 5 of the 21 chapters: the core idea, trade-offs, the 90 percent rule, saying no and cutting losses. The rest adds stories around them.

entry.title: Mindset: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 3 of the 8 chapters: the 2 mindsets, how they change failure and effort, and how to change yours. The middle chapters apply the idea to sport, work, love and parenting. Chapters follow the updated edition.

entry.title: Man's Search for Meaning: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 3 of the 6 parts: Frankl's camp memoir, his short guide to logotherapy and the 1984 postscript. The book is short, so read them in order. Parts follow the 2006 Beacon Press edition.

entry.title: The ONE Thing: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 4 of the 18 chapters: the success list, the focusing question, goal setting to the now and time blocking. The rest repeats the 1 idea with stories and research.

entry.title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 5 of the 13 sections: Inside-Out, Habits 1, 2 and 3, and Habit 5. The rest is useful but long. Sections follow the original contents; newer editions add notes by Sean Covey.

entry.title: The Total Money Makeover: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 4 of the 13 chapters: debt myths, the $1,000 starter fund, the debt snowball and the full emergency fund. The rest follows the same plan through US retirement, college and mortgage steps.

entry.title: The Millionaire Next Door: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 3 of the 8 chapters: meet the millionaire, frugal, and you aren't what you drive. The data is from 1990s US surveys, but the pattern still holds.

entry.title: The Courage to Be Disliked: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 3 of the 7 parts: the first 3 nights. They hold Adler's core ideas: your past doesn't decide your life, most problems are about other people, and their opinion of you is their task. The book is a dialogue, so it reads fast. Parts follow the 2018 English edition.

entry.title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 4 of the 9 chapters: don't try, the value of suffering, you are always choosing, and the importance of saying no. The rest makes the same case with more stories.

entry.title: The Willpower Instinct: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 5 of the 9 chapters: 1, 4, 5, 6 and 9. They explain why you give in and what to do in the moment. The others are worth a skim for 1 experiment each.

entry.title: The Craving Mind: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 3 of the 10 chapters: 1, 2 and 5. They explain the loop behind every habit and show it in your phone and your own thinking. The rest applies the same idea to other cravings.

entry.title: Rest: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 4 of the 13 chapters: 4 Hours, Walk, Stop and Recovery. They cover how much focused work a day is enough, and how to rest so you come back sharper. The rest adds stories and research to the same case.

entry.title: Make Time: which parts to read
entry.summary: Read 4 of the 10 sections: How Make Time Works, Highlight, Highlight Tactics and Laser Tactics. They give you the daily method and the best tactics to protect it. Skim the rest for 1 or 2 ideas.
